prompt.en: A student has ₹100 and must choose between buying a notebook now or saving the money towards a tennis racket later. Which economic concept best explains this situation? Name the concept and explain why it applies here. (3 marks)

label.en: Correctly names opportunity cost as the concept at work

level1.en: Whichever way the ₹100 goes, what exactly does the student lose? The chapter has a name for that loss.

clue.en: It is the idea Riya met behind the two doors: the best option she said no to.

level2Template.en: The economic concept that explains this situation is ___.

label.en: States its meaning — the value of the next-best alternative given up when a choice is made

level1.en: Is the real cost just the ₹100 note — or something else? Remember, the ₹100 leaves the pocket either way.

clue.en: Opportunity cost is not the money spent; it is whichever single unchosen option disappears.

level2Template.en: Opportunity cost is the value of the ___ alternative sacrificed when a choice is made.

label.en: Applies it to both sides of the scenario — choosing the notebook makes the delayed racket the cost, and saving for the racket means doing without the notebook

level1.en: Say the student buys the notebook: state precisely what was sacrificed. Now say the student saves instead: what is sacrificed then?

clue.en: Each route has its own invisible price tag: notebook chosen, racket postponed; racket fund chosen, pages unwritten.

level2Template.en: If the notebook is bought, the postponed ___ constitutes the opportunity cost of the decision.

text.en: The situation described above illustrates how every choice imposes a real cost upon the decision-maker.
The economic concept that explains this situation is ___.
Opportunity cost is the value of the ___ alternative sacrificed when a choice is made.
If the notebook is bought, the postponed ___ constitutes the opportunity cost of the decision.
